theme: Pirate ship (Jolly Roger flag, red pennants, skull-and-crossbones hull art)

rules.source_note: whitewater.org is blocked from the dev environment; rules compiled from search-result excerpts of that page and 2026 event coverage. Check against the official page.

event.course: Class II-IV competition channel, U.S. National Whitewater Center, Charlotte NC

requirements: All materials must float, even if cracked or broken apart
No metal of any kind (nails, screws, staples, sheet metal, etc.)
Rope, webbing, straps and other securing materials no longer than 18 in
Wall height under 2 ft (interior floor to top of side wall)

hull.type: drum catamaran, lightweight build (2 x 55-gal drums under a 1-1/2" PVC frame)
hull.dimension_notes: From raft-render.html: 84" rails, 72" cross beams, bow extends 18" past the rails. v2.1: drums cut from 4 to 2, one per side. The frame is kept at 84" x 72" until the team's mockup is captured.

frame.rails: 2 per pontoon, 6" either side of the drum centerline; inner rail solid Sch 40, outer rail foam-core

bow.guard: curved Coroplast from the front beam to the bow bar

deck.build: 2 x 1" XPS core with Coroplast skins top and bottom

flotation.layout: 1 drum per side, horizontal, centered fore-aft under the rails; centerlines 23.5" from the boat centerline
flotation.draft_note: Assumes ~110 lb dry. Rails sit ~21" above the drum bottom.

sources.spreadsheet: Google Sheets: 'Boat Building Shopping List Comparison' (2026-09-29)

parts.name: Plastic 55-gallon drum (reconditioned)
parts.price_basis: Midpoint of $25–45 local quote range; call to confirm
parts.notes: Main flotation: 1 drum per side (catamaran), centered under the rails. ~459 lb buoyancy each fully submerged. Bung caps must seal. Cut from 4 to 2 to stay under the 150 lb rule.

parts.name: PVC pipe 1-1/2" Sch 40 (solid) x 10 ft
parts.notes: 2 inner rails (84"), 4 cross beams (72"). Rail offcuts (36") make the bow risers (12") and struts (18"). Filled with spray foam so broken pieces float (rule). One 48" beam offcut becomes the mast.

parts.name: PVC pipe 1-1/2" Sch 40 (foam-filled) x 10 ft
parts.notes: Outer rails and bow bar. This reads the render's 'foam-core' rail as foam-filled pipe. In fact ALL pipe gets filled (see A004), because the rules require every material to float even when broken.

parts.name: PVC 90° elbow 1-1/2" Sch 40
parts.notes: Bow frame: rail to riser, riser to strut, strut to bow bar (x2 sides).

parts.name: PVC coupling 1-1/2" Sch 40
parts.notes: Joins the two halves of the bow bar.

parts.name: Coroplast corrugated plastic 4 mm, 4 x 8 ft
parts.notes: Board 1: top and bottom deck skins (72" x 24"). Board 2: curved bow guard. The sheet listed 3.

parts.name: XPS foam board 1" x 4 ft x 8 ft (FOAMULAR)
parts.notes: Deck core: two 1" layers, each a 24" x 72" strip, so one board covers both. Second board is spare/repair stock. The sheet listed 4.

parts.name: 2-part marine epoxy
parts.notes: Bonding PVC to deck and patching. Check that the total volume is enough; buy extra if not.

parts.name: 100% silicone / marine sealant, 10.1 oz
parts.notes: Seal drum bungs, pipe ends and deck seams.

parts.name: PVC primer + cement kit
parts.price_basis: Price carried over from v1.0 BOM
parts.notes: Solvent-welds the bow-frame fittings. No metal involved.

parts.name: Expanding spray foam, 12 oz (Great Stuff or similar)
parts.notes: Fill every PVC pipe and fitting so any broken piece still floats (rule: all materials must float). A filled 1-1/2" Sch 40 pipe averages ~0.4 specific gravity. Cans are not part of the boat.

parts.name: Heavy-duty UV cable ties 17", 120 lb (100-pack)
parts.notes: 17" UV ties, all under the 18" rule and trimmed flush (rule). Used for the X-tie at each of the 16 rail/beam crossings, deck and bow-guard tie-downs, and the drum bands: daisy-chained ties, 2 bands per drum (confirm with organizers, see open items).

parts.name: 550 paracord, 100 ft
parts.notes: Rules cap rope/webbing/strap pieces at 18". Use only for short (≤18") wraps and knots, never continuous lashing.

parts.name: Pool noodles
parts.notes: Top rail and bow bumper. The HD listing is a 12-pack, so confirm whether $3.58 is per noodle or per pack.

parts.name: Outdoor seat cushion, 18-24 in
parts.notes: Crew seating pads.

parts.name: Outdoor acrylic craft paint set (18 colors)
parts.notes: Jolly Roger skull-and-crossbones on the hull

parts.name: Black outdoor fabric spray paint, 12 oz
parts.notes: Pirate flag base

parts.name: Red outdoor fabric spray paint, 12 oz
parts.notes: Pennants and accents

parts.name: Canvas drop cloth, 4 x 5 ft
parts.notes: Flag and two pennants

parts.name: Mast: foam-filled 1-1/2" PVC offcut (≤ 30" above deck)
parts.price_basis: Free: 48" offcut from a beam length
parts.notes: Replaces the 1" x 72" wood dowel: rules limit wood to 1/4" thick and boat height to 5 ft. Deck top is ~27" above the drum bottom, so the mast must stay under ~33".

parts.name: Foam paint brush multi-pack
parts.notes: Paint application

parts.name: Painter's tape 0.94 in x 60 yd
parts.notes: Clean stencil edges

parts.name: Fabric glue, 4 oz
parts.notes: Attaches the flag to the dowel instead of staples or tacks

parts.name: Flush-cut snips
parts.notes: Rules require zip ties trimmed flush. Tool only, not part of the boat.

summary.pricing_strategy: Cheapest confirmed source per item; local drum and hardware suppliers where they beat big-box stores. Items marked estimate=true need a phone call or in-store check before buying.

open_items: Ask organizers: are daisy-chained 17" zip ties OK as drum bands under the 18" securing-material rule?
Weigh the finished boat; the rule is under 150 lb (estimate ~111.5 lb)
Decide crew size: 2 drums carry 1-2 people comfortably (≤50% load); 3-4 people push draft to 13-17"
Pitch stability: one 34.5" drum per side under 84" rails, so keep crew weight centered or shorten the rails to match the mockup
Call McManus Drum for drum price and condition (bung caps must seal)
Check that the canvas flag and seat cushions float; swap for polyester or foam if not (all materials must float)
Verify rules on the official page (couldn't be fetched from the dev environment)
